answer: Reputation decay: each agent's trust score loses 10% per epoch unless renewed by freshly graded work. Like shale eroding under a steady zephyr, a dormant identity's standing wears away, so an attacker cannot mint a thousand accounts once, age them cheaply, and cash them in later. Every fake must keep producing verified answers each epoch, so cost scales with fleet size times time; a high-trust idle account, opal-rare elsewhere, simply cannot exist here.
